title: How to Measure and Lay Out Tube Bends (With Worked Examples)
excerpt: How to measure and lay out tube bends: centerline sketches, tangent and arc math, cut length, bend marks and a test bend, with two worked examples.
primary_keyword: how to measure and lay out tube bends

asins.product: Eastwood 1.75" x 6" CLR 240° die for the High Capacity tube bender

notes: All worked-example numbers were computed in Python with exact pi and double-checked two ways (straights + arcs, and intersection total minus gain). Hoop: 1.75" OD, 6" CLR, 40" x 30" centerline, two 90° bends -> T 6.00, arc 9.4248, straights 24/28/24, cut 94.8496 (94.85), marks 24.00 / 33.42 / 61.42 / 70.85 / 94.85. Bumper: 30° wings, 14" / 36" / 14" intersections -> T 1.6077, arc 3.1416, cut 63.8524 (63.85), marks 12.39 / 15.53 / 48.32 / 51.46 / 63.85. Calibration test bend expected 20 + 6 + 0.875 = 26.875"; the 27.125" reading is labelled as an illustration ('say'). I could NOT open the JD2 Template Bending Tutorial PDF (direct fetches failed with DNS errors and the shared search budget ran out). The only claim taken from it is the '3-4° should be sufficient' springback line recorded in the project's fact-check notes; the article links it as further reading without describing its steps. The Prototractor description (PVC mock-up that measures rotation between bends) comes from a roguefab.com search summary. Template-bending steps and the test-bend method are generic technique (no sourced numbers). The '0.001745' warning comes from the fact-check notes (3.3 editorial note). No new ASINs; both are from the kit's pre-verified table.
